questions.question: A relationship involving three or more entity types.
questions.explanation: Ternary relationships connect three entities, like supplier-part-project relationships.

questions.question: An alternative data modeling notation to ER diagrams.
questions.explanation: UML class diagrams can model database structures with classes, attributes, and associations.

questions.question: A design pattern where a generalized entity is specialized into subtypes.
questions.explanation: Generalization models hierarchical relationships where subtypes inherit from supertypes.

questions.question: Constraint where a subtype entity must belong to exactly one supertype.
questions.explanation: Disjoint constraints ensure an entity instance belongs to at most one subtype.

questions.question: Constraint allowing a subtype entity to belong to multiple supertypes.
questions.explanation: Overlapping constraints permit entity instances to belong to multiple subtypes simultaneously.

questions.question: Whether every supertype instance must be a member of some subtype.
questions.explanation: Completeness constraints specify if all supertype entities must belong to a subtype (total) or not (partial).

questions.question: A relationship where an entity relates to itself.
questions.explanation: Recursive relationships model hierarchies like employee-manager or prerequisite courses.

questions.question: The process of mapping an ER model to relational tables.
questions.explanation: ER-to-relational mapping transforms entities and relationships into table structures.

questions.question: An attribute that helps distinguish instances in a weak entity.
questions.explanation: Partial keys uniquely identify weak entity instances when combined with the owner entity's key.

questions.question: A notation that uses crow's foot symbols to show relationship cardinality.
questions.explanation: Crow's foot notation uses graphical symbols to represent cardinality constraints in ER diagrams.

questions.question: In ER-to-relational mapping, a multivalued attribute is converted into this.
questions.explanation: Each multivalued attribute becomes its own relation keyed by the owner key plus the value.

questions.question: The relationship type that links a weak entity to its owner entity.
questions.explanation: A weak entity is identified through its identifying relationship with the owner entity.

questions.question: Labels assigned to an entity's participations to clarify the meaning of a recursive relationship.
questions.explanation: Role names (e.g., supervisor, supervisee) disambiguate recursive participations.

questions.question: The extended ER model that adds subclasses, specialization, generalization, and categories.
questions.explanation: EER extends basic ER with supertype/subtype hierarchies and categories.

questions.question: An EER construct for a subclass that is a subset of the union of multiple superclasses.
questions.explanation: A category (union type) draws members from several different superclasses.
